name: Remington electric shavers

card.summary: Foil and rotary electric shavers from the Remington brand for a quick, clean-shaven or neatly trimmed face.

quick.overview:
Remington is a long-running brand of electric shavers, trimmers and grooming appliances. Men use them to keep the face clean-shaven or the beard edged without wet-shaving gear.

The brand's shaver line began in 1937 and its best-known pitch, from owner Victor Kiam, was a close shave as a blade [1]. No clinical research concerns the brand itself.
quick.how: Users shave dry or with a pre-shave product, moving the foil or rotary head over the skin. Trimmers handle beard length and edges. Heads and foils are replaced periodically according to maker guidance.
quick.risks: Electric shavers can cause razor burn or irritation in some users. Forum users compare electric and blade shaving on closeness and comfort, with mixed opinions about individual brands [2].

lead: Remington is a brand of personal-care appliances best known for electric shavers. The name comes from E. Remington and Sons, a firearms maker founded in 1816; Remington Rand began making electric shavers in 1937, starting with the Model E [1].

People use electric shavers to remove facial hair quickly or keep a short beard tidy, which is a basic part of grooming and facial presentation. The brand also sells hair clippers, beard and nose/ear trimmers, epilators and hair-care tools [1].

In 1979 Victor Kiam acquired the shaver business in a leveraged buyout and fronted its TV advertising with the slogan 'Shaves as close as a blade, or your money back!' The brand is now owned by Spectrum Brands [1].

chain: Electric foil or rotary shaving head
Removes or trims facial hair quickly
angle.text: A shaver keeps stubble off the face or maintains a clean beard line. Trimmer attachments allow a set length.

paras: Remington Rand began producing electric shavers in 1937. Sperry Rand kept the line after the 1955 merger. Victor Kiam bought it in 1979, and Kiam's company acquired Clairol's personal-care appliance business in 1994. Vestar Capital Partners bought control in 1996, and Rayovac (later Spectrum Brands) purchased the company in 2003 [1].
Men's and women's shavers, hair clippers, beard and nose/ear trimmers, epilators, hair-care tools and foot massagers [1].

A 2002 T Nation thread comparing electric razors to blades includes one user who praised a competitor's shaver and called an older Remington unsatisfactory, illustrating that opinions about brands are personal and varied [2].

timeline.event: Remington Rand starts making electric shavers [1]
Victor Kiam acquires the shaver business [1]
Sold to Rayovac, later Spectrum Brands [1]
